patch.summary:
Thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — Close documents a broader use-case set; Mailchimp is narrower/specialist.

Comparison thesis: General-purpose vs specialist. Choose Close only if your buying job matches “Sales-focused CRM for pipeline management and sales engagement workflows.” rather than Mailchimp's shape. Choose Mailchimp only if your buying job matches “Email marketing with CRM features; freemium entry (secondary category: marketing).” rather than Close's shape. Workflow advantage: Close leans pipeline-management, sales-engagement; Mailchimp leans lead-management, contact-management. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — Close documents a broader use-case set; Mailchimp is narrower/specialist.
- Positioning: Close is Sales-focused CRM for pipeline management and sales engagement workflows.; Mailchimp is Email marketing with CRM features; freemium entry (secondary category: marketing)..
- Workflow coverage skew: Close-leaning pipeline-management, sales-engagement, email-outreach vs Mailchimp-leaning lead-management, contact-management, inbound-sales.
- Researched limits: Close — Growth ($99 annual) and Scale ($139 annual) per-user pricing is high versus pipeline-only CRMs; calling usage and premium phone lines add cost.; Mailchimp — Marketing-led CRM — not a full sales pipeline platform.

Limitations — Close: Growth ($99 annual) and Scale ($139 annual) per-user pricing is high versus pipeline-only CRMs; calling usage and premium phone lines add cost.; Advanced Chloe automation/workflows and predictive dialing depth are concentrated on Growth and Scale.; Mailchimp: Marketing-led CRM — not a full sales pipeline platform; Paid pricing is contact-based and changes — verify live.

Poor-fit cases: Close is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Growth ($99 annual) and Scale ($139 annual) per-user pricing is high versus pipeline-only CRMs; calling usage and premium phone lines add cost. · Mailchimp is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Marketing-led CRM — not a full sales pipeline platform · Avoid Close if you actually need Mailchimp's motion (Email marketing with CRM features; freemium entry (secondary category: marketing)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
